name: Screened-Kinetic Decoupling via Lapse-Weighted Preferred-Frame Sector
claimed_mechanism: It introduces a local lapse-weighted multiplier alpha = e^{-y} that couples only to the preferred-frame constraint sector, while the propagating scalar phi carries an independent kinetic normalization K0. The frozen mu(y)=1-e^{-y} controls the MOND interpolation, but alpha is not used to normalize the phi kinetic term, so the screened preferred-frame response and the finite propagating-mode kinetic normalization are canonically separated. Matter remains minimally coupled to the single metric, and no rescaling of G is introduced.
predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field limit the metric is g00 = -1 + 2 Phi/c^2 with Phi = Phi_N + Phi_M. The MOND correction Phi_M is generated by the frozen mu(y)=1-e^{-y} through the auxiliary interpolation variable, so the acceleration interpolates between Newtonian and MOND behavior. The preferred-frame anisotropic term is multiplied by alpha = e^{-y}, so it is exponentially suppressed in high-density systems, while the phi mode keeps a finite speed and finite kinetic normalization K0.
inequivalence_argument: This is not a coefficient tweak of a killed architecture because the canonical structure changes: the preferred-frame response is carried by a lapse-weighted multiplier in the constraint sector, whereas the propagating scalar kinetic term is an independent standard kinetic term with its own normalization. It is inequivalent to degenerate khronon-only models because phi is a propagating degree of freedom with finite kinetic normalization, and inequivalent to nonlocal F+ constructions because all couplings are local and no spatial integral operator appears. It also differs from constraint-first q architectures by making the screened preferred-frame multiplier, not a constraint variable, the object that carries the e^{-y} suppression, while preserving a single metric and minimal matter coupling.
